fixes.explanation: Fear is a fair guess, but the text doesn't go there. The writer says it is hard to explain “…because you are dull of hearing.” He's talking about how they take in what he says, not what they're scared of. So the problem is their listening, baker, not their nerves.
Close, baker, but it's the other way around. The writer says to these readers, “You need milk, not solid food!” So he's telling them they aren't ready for solid food yet. They need the basics first.

An infant, baker. The writer says everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness. Milk is where an infant starts, and the writer says solid food is for the mature. It's a picture of someone who still has growing to do.

Good from evil, baker. The writer says the mature “…by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.” It's practice that does it, not a one-time lesson. Like me and my stamping: the first batch came out a mess, and now I press clean without thinking.

If God permits, baker. The writer says, “And this we will do, if God permits.” I think he's saying the going on depends on God, not on how fired up they feel. A good baker still checks with the One who owns the kitchen.
A vote sounds tidy, friend, but the writer never mentions one. He says, “And this we will do, if God permits.” The condition he gives is God, not the church's agreement.

That's what the writer says, baker. These people are “…crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.” Those are heavy words, and I think they ought to feel heavy. This is a hard part of the passage.

Idols aren't in this verse, baker. The writer's reason is that they are “…crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.” That's the reason he gives. It's a heavy part of the passage.
Burned, baker. The writer says the land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. Then he adds, “In the end it will be burned.” It's a sobering picture.

Wealth is not what he says, friend. The writer says, “He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name…” It's their work that counts here, not their bank account. I'm a stamper who came with a 25 cent sticker, so that sounds just right to me.
